To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the environment is a critical determinant of the ability of people to communicate effectively; (2) the environment is the key to improving the quality of communication between people with a communication disability and their health care providers in acute care hospitals; and (3) the environment is also the key to improving communication between people with any type of communication disability and their care providers.

the literature on communication between people with specific types and people with multiple communication disabilities and their health care providers in acute hospital settings indicates that there are a number of environmental factors that facilitate and/or create barriers to communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the environmental factors that can be modified to improve the communication between healthcare providers in the hospital setting and people with communication disabilities.
the environmental factors that can facilitate or create barriers to communication between people with different types communication disabilities and their health care providers.

the identification of the environmental factors that affect communication between people with different types and severities of communication disabilities and healthcare providers in acute care settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the literature is not conclusive and that there is a need for more research to identify the environmental factors that are most important in acute hospitals that facilitate or create communication barriers for people with different types and severities of communication disabilities when interacting with their healthcare providers.

the environmental factors that have the most influence on the communication between people with a communication disability and their health care providers are the communication strategies used, the communication environment, and the attitudes of the people who are communicating.

there is an urgent need for research into environmental factors that facilitate communication between adults with a wide range of communication disabilities and healthcare providers in the context of acute hospital settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

environmental factors can be identified in acute hospital environments that can facilitate or create barriers to effective communication between people with different types communication disabilities and their health care providers.

the environmental factors in acute care hospitals that facilitate or create communication barriers are those which influence the accessibility and acceptability of the environment, the availability of communication supports, and the communication skills of healthcare providers.

the environmental factors that have the greatest impact on communication between people with specific types and degrees of communication disability and their hospital-based healthcare providers are those that are related to the healthcare system, the healthcare providers themselves and the physical environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environment in acute care hospitals needs to be more accessible communicatively for all people, including people with communication disabilities.
the environment of the acute care hospital is not a neutral one for communication.

there is a need for more research into the influence of the environment on the communication between people with specific communication disabilities and their health-care providers, in order that the environment can be modified to facilitate communication between people with different types and levels of communication disability and their health-care provider.
